newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz insurer sticks to bullish outlook.
newsitem.headline: Allianz insurer sticks to bullish outlook.

text.p: Europe's leading insurance group, Allianz AG Holding, Monday said it was still on track for record earnings this year after income from premiums rose 8.3 percent in the first six months of 1996.

Henning Schulte-Noelle, chairman of the Munich-based insurer, told Allianz's annual shareholder meeting that overall foreign business had been buoyant so far despite price pressures plaguing the German market.
"Your company is progressing well. We are making particular progress towards strengthening our earnings power," Schulte-Noelle said.
Schulte-Noelle said he expected a considerable boost in pre-tax earnings in 1996 but added his customary caveat that progress depended on claims and capital market developments.
Allianz's pretax earnings surged 34.4 percent to a record 3.04 billion marks ($1.99 billion) in 1995 and Schulte-Noelle has in the past forecast another double-digit rise in earnings this year.

But the group does not see net earnings keeping pace with the pre-tax figure. Allianz's net profit of 2.02 billion marks ($1.32 billion) in 1995, boosted sharply by one-time tax breaks related to its east German business.
Allianz's business has been plagued in the past year by stiff price competition for auto insurance in its newly deregulated home market.

But foreign business compensated, especially on the life insurance side. Allianz said its non-German European life and health insurance premiums rose as much as 28 percent in the first six months of the year.
The forecasts do not allow for any effects of possible consolidation of new units. Allianz is expected to shortly complete its takeover of the Vereinte Gruppe, Europe's second-largest health insurer.
